item.text: I found one remaining structural cleanup that’s actually useful: the sorter still computes each bucket index twice, once for counting and again for distribution. I’m folding validation and index planning into one internal plan object so the pipeline stays linear and the second pass only scatters values.

I’m cleaning up the internal layout now. The current version still exposes boundary storage to the outer method, so I’m encapsulating the planned bucket indexes and boundary offsets behind a single immutable plan type.

The sorter now carries one internal distribution plan instead of recomputing bucket indexes during scatter. I’m adding one more rejection case for negative infinity, then I’ll verify the build and tests again.
I’ve finished the refactor and test update. Compiling and running the demo plus the test harness now to confirm the new distribution plan behaves the same.

Refactored [BucketSort.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/039_bucket_sort/BucketSort.java:1) to use a single internal `DistributionPlan` instead of recomputing bucket indexes during both counting and scattering. Validation, per-value bucket assignment, and bucket boundary construction now happen in one place, and the scatter phase just follows the precomputed plan. That keeps the current flat-array design but removes duplicated bucket-index logic.

I also extended [BucketSortTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/039_bucket_sort/BucketSortTest.java:1) with explicit `Float.NEGATIVE_INFINITY` coverage so the non-finite input contract is tested on both sides.

Verified with:

- `java Main`
